core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 7806-7813): the equality H^n_{Zar}(X, pi_X^{-1}F) = H^n(X, F) is a general fact following from the trivial observation that coverings in LC_Zar are refinements of ordinary coverings of X, so the two cohomologies are computed by the same Cech complexes.

Parts (2) and (3) (proof lines 7816-7826): pi_{X,*} = tau_X^{-1} for the morphism of topoi tau_X : Sh(X_Zar) -> Sh(LC_Zar) provided by the comparison of a site with a bigger site, which gives exactness of pi_{X,*}; and tau_X^{-1} pi_X^{-1} is the identity functor, which gives that the unit of the adjunction is an isomorphism.
Part (4) (statement with the proofs of (1)-(3)): the derived statement for K in D(X) follows from the exactness of pi_{X,*} and the identity of the composite on the level of the unit.

Part (5) (proof lines 7832-7839): the morphism of topoi f_{Zar} is obtained from the relocalization result, applied to the continuous functor sending an object Z/Y to Z x_Y X/X, and the square of topoi commutes by construction.

Part (6) (proof lines 7842-7851): using the same-chapter computation of cohomology on open subschemes one rewrites H^n_{Zar}(X, pi_Y^{-1}G) as H^n_{Zar}(X, f_{Zar}^{-1}pi_Y^{-1}G) and then applies parts (1) and (5).

Part (7a) (proof lines 7854-7883): for a sheaf F on X and an object g : Z -> Y of LC_Zar/Y, the fibred square is used to compute both sides on sections over Z, which gives pi_Y^{-1}f_*F = f_{Zar,*}pi_X^{-1}F.

Part (7b) (proof lines 7886-7915): for K in D^+(X) the same computation is redone on the level of higher direct images using the presheaf description of Rf_{Zar,*}, which upgrades the identification to the derived statement.
proof_roadmap: Part (1): coverings in LC_Zar refine ordinary coverings, so the Cech complexes agree.
Parts (2) and (3): identify pi_{X,*} with the inverse image of the comparison morphism tau_X, then use that tau_X^{-1}pi_X^{-1} is the identity.
Part (5): build f_{Zar} from the relocalization result applied to the functor Z/Y maps to Z x_Y X/X.
Part (6): rewrite one side by the computation of cohomology on an open subscheme and apply parts (1) and (5).
Parts (7a) and (7b): compare sections over an object of LC_Zar/Y through the fibred square, first for sheaves and then for higher direct images.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects the comparison results between the Zariski topoi of the big site of locally quasi-compact spaces and the small Zariski topoi of a space, in seven numbered items covering cohomology, exactness of the pushforward, the unit of the adjunction, the derived statement, the commutativity of the square induced by a morphism f : X -> Y, and the base change identities for a proper f (statement lines 7769-7804). Each item is proved separately in the counted span: parts (1)-(3) are read off from the comparison of a site with a bigger site and from the identity of the composite tau_X^{-1} pi_X^{-1} (proof lines 7806-7826), part (5) is built from the relocalization result (proof lines 7832-7839), part (6) combines the computation of cohomology on open subschemes with the previous parts (proof lines 7842-7851), and parts (7a) and (7b) compare both sides on sections over an object of LC_Zar/Y using the fibred square, the derived case being handled through the presheaf description of the higher direct images (proof lines 7854-7915). The claim is H2: seven short arguments of the same flavour, each written out, with the derived case as the most technical.
